answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may claim rewards from a task. A beacon can publish unpredictable task assignments, while a prism-style audit samples completed work and checks it against independent evidence; proven duplicate or fabricated claims burn the deposit. A vertex in the reputation graph gains influence only through costly, verified contributions, not by creating neighbors. A sybil attacker must therefore tie up capital per identity and risks losing it, making mass fake accounts expensive rather than free.
